paraphrase: Dharma is expounded in (Jaimini's) work of twelve 'marks' (chapters), namely: means of knowledge, distinction, subsidiarity, prompting, sequence, eligibility, transfer in general and in particular, modification, cancellation, single performance (tantra) and incidental benefit (prasaṅga), in that order.
notes: Checked against the local e-text of the Jaiminīya-nyāya-mālā-vistara.

paraphrase: Each topic (adhikaraṇa) has five members: the subject (viṣaya), the doubt (sandeha), the connection (saṅgati), the prima facie view (pūrvapakṣa) and the conclusion (siddhānta); the connection is threefold — with the whole śāstra, the chapter and the quarter — and can be worked out by the reader; usually one verse gives subject, doubt and prima facie view, and another the conclusion.
notes: Checked against the local e-text of the Jaiminīya-nyāya-mālā-vistara. Paraphrase follows the author's own prose (MJAINYC 1.1.7 and 1.1.10); no original because of an e-text misprint.
